text:
Evan: quick design follow-up from last week's pool sync. idea: replace ad-hoc burst credits with a small per-tenant "burst ledger" service that does token-bucket style admission + a reconciliation window. would reduce operator cross-talk and make throttles predictable. thoughts?

Ruth: sounds promising. two immediate Qs: 1) where is the ledger authoritative (control-plane vs shim vs operator)? 2) how do we surface fast failure to clients when a tenant is out of burst tokens?

Evan: plan is ledger in control-plane (APIs only), operator polls ledger for active grants. ledger returns grants with a lease_id and an expiry. clients see a 429 + Retry-After when ledger denies. operator will still keep local safety checks.

Carlos: ok, but polling latency is a concern. if operator polls every 10s we could miss short bursts. can we include a small push channel or websocket for hot leases?

Maya: +1 to push. alternate: let ledger hand out a short-lived fast-path token (opaque string) that client includes in request. operator validates token locally (signed JWT) to skip ledger lookup for a few seconds.

Zoe: love the signed token idea. security note: tokens must be HMAC-signed with a key rotation plan. also add a usage_nonce so operator can detect replay within the TTL.

Evan: sketch of grant proto we discussed:

```
grant = {
  "tenant": "acme",
  "lease_id": "g-2026-01-15-01",
  "tokens": 5,
  "fast_token": "eyJ...",
  "ttl": 30,   # seconds
  "epoch": 7
}
```

Carlos: how does operator behave if it receives two conflicting grants for same node capacity? e.g., local packing says no, ledger says yes and wants eviction.

Maya: propose operator modes: 
- advisory (default): operator uses grants to prewarm but won't evict running jobs;
- strict: operator guarantees grant by evicting non-critical jobs and honoring tenant priority.
Also config per-pool and per-tenant.

Ruth: defaults make sense. add a third "soft-reserve" mode where operator will reserve headroom by refusing non-reserved admits, instead of evicting. less disruptive.

Evan: good call. three-mode matrix: advisory, soft-reserve, strict. admin knob via tenant profile + pool policy. we'll document tradeoffs.

Zoe: observability hooks: ledger_emit(grant_issued, grant_denied, grant_revoked), operator_emit(grant_applied, grant_conflict, grant_drift_seconds). add a grafana dashboard for per-tenant burst burn rate.

Carlos: we need safety when ledger/CP and operator disagree after a partition. reconciliation rules: operator should prefer local state if last-seen-epoch > grant. and ledger should include epoch so operator can compare. if mismatch, operator emits grant_conflict and uses local safety.

Maya: plus a reconciliation backoff: operator will retry applying a grant for N attempts spread over TTL, then give up and emit drift. avoids hammering eviction.

Evan: rollout plan: 1) ledger prototype behind FF, 2) add fast-token path to SDK (opt-in), 3) canary on single shard with advisory mode only, 4) enable soft-reserve for beta tenants, 5) strict mode for contracted reservations.

Ruth: ops checklist for canary: make sure we can revoke grants cleanly, export grant-related traces, simulate ledger partition and ensure clients get clear 429s.

ops-bot: canary-deploy: burst-ledger:v0.1 -> staging-shard-2 (mode=advisory) :white_check_mark: 

Carlos: one more: cost accounting. ledger should attach a cost_estimate for granted tokens so billing can attribute burst spend. small scalar per-token is fine.

Zoe: agree. also add a tenant-level daily_quota for burst tokens to avoid runaway spend. ledger should enforce both token bucket and budget.

Maya: implementation note: fast-token validation should be constant-time and avoid network calls. HMAC+nonce window stored in operator memory with small LRU should be enough.

Evan: thanks everyone. i'll spin a short RFC with the grant proto, operator modes table, rollout stages, and an SE-facing FAQ (how to choose advisory vs soft vs strict). will attach example SDK snippets for fast-token usage.

Ruth: please cc eng-oncall and billing when RFC is up.

Carlos: excited to test on embedding spikes :rocket:

Zoe: adding a doc task to the backlog for the grafana dashboard.
